NACL margins expected to stabilize around 9% to 10% next year from 6% to 7% currently as product portfolio changes.

Impairment taken on Dhaksha drone business investments and goodwill due to long lead times in order execution.
FY26 subsidy receipts totaled ₹10,649 Cr, while outstanding subsidy stood at ₹2,168 Cr at March end.

operating_notes.text: Commissioned 2,000 TPD Sulphuric Acid and 650 TPD Phosphoric Acid plants at Kakinada with ~₹1,100 Cr outlay.
Crop Protection business recorded 16% revenue growth and 55% profitability growth in FY26.
Agri Retail network scaled to 1,200 centers with over 300 stores added in FY26.
Phosphoric Acid price fixed at USD 1,360/t vs USD 1,290/t previously; Ammonia and Sulphur trading around $800-$850.
Holding 71.5% stake in Senegalese rock phosphate mining entity BMCC.
Finished fertilizer inventory stood at ~5.5 lakh tons at the end of March 2026.
Fertilizer production was 6.9 lakh tons in Q1FY27 versus 8.4 lakh tons a year ago, about 72% capacity utilisation.
Phosphoric acid for Q2 settled at $1,700 a tonne versus $1,360 in Q1.
Subsidy outstanding was ₹3,254 Cr at 30 June 2026, with ₹568 Cr received in July.

timeline.summary: Coromandel International Limited’s Board, led by **AN Balasubramanian** and **B Shanmugasundaram**, declared a final dividend of ₹2 per equity share on May 7, 2026, payable by August 21, 2026, with a record date of July 16, 2026.
Coromandel International reported FY26 consolidated Total Income of ₹31,827 Cr (up 30% YoY) and commissioned its ₹1,100 Cr acid plants in Kakinada.

Coromandel International Limited’s **B. Shanmugasundaram**, **Balasubramanian Anian Shanmugasundaram**, and **Shanmugasu M** uploaded Q4FY26 investor presentation on May 8, 2026, per SEBI’s Reg 46(2)(o).
Coromandel held its Q4FY26 earnings call highlighting severe Middle East raw material cost pressure for Q2 and commissioning of its Kakinada acid plants.
Coromandel's Q1FY27 call (24 July 2026) reported revenue up 15% to ₹8,215 Cr but EBITDA down 3% to ₹761 Cr and PAT at ₹382 Cr; as input costs outran the NBS subsidy revision.
Additional Commissioner, Office Of The Commissioner, Vadodara-II, Central GST passed an order demanding Rs. 2,50,82,496 for FY 2021-22 to FY 2024-25.
Deputy Commissioner (Appeal), Chennai North, Tamil Nadu State GST passed an order for FY 2019-20, demanding tax Rs.1,78,56,068, interest Rs.2,08,43,168, penalty Rs.17,85,606.
